scope: Corollary 6.3 (The sharp complete inequality for bounded operators) of the manuscript “The complete Crouzeix theorem: optimal similarity and a common positive boundary representation” (preprints/The-complete-Crouzeix-theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 325 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b5e37fffcae2be84), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let H be a complex Hilbert space, with no separability assumption, and let A ∈ B(H). Suppose first that H ̸= {0}, and put W(A) = {⟨x, Ax⟩ : x ∈ H, ∥x∥ = 1}, K = W(A). Then K is compact and convex and contains spec(A). For every positive integer m, every nonnegative integer d, and every matrix polynomial P(z) = Pd k=0 Bkzk with Bk ∈ Mm(C), the operator P[A] = Pd k=0 Ak ⊗ Bk on H ⊗ Cm satisfies ∥P[A]∥ ≤ 2 sup z∈W(A) ∥P(z)∥ = 2 max z∈K ∥P(z)∥. (6.1) More generally, if U is an open neighborhood of K and F = (fij) : U → Mm(C) is holomorphic, its entrywise holomorphic evaluation, in the same base-first tensor convention, satisfies F[A] := m X i,j=1 fij(A) ⊗ Eij, ∥F[A]∥ ≤ 2 max z∈K ∥F(z)∥. (6.2)
